public_rationale: Contemporary controlled experiments support the practical claim that tool-free LLM multiplication remained unreliable, especially beyond training complexity. Successful priming shows that progress was possible, but it does not demonstrate reliable multiplication at lengths wholly excluded from training. This supports continuing unreliability, not the stronger assertion that neural models never learn algorithms or cannot improve.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading remain stuck as continuing unreliability rather than no progress.
Finite behavioral tests do not establish an architectural impossibility.
The findings concern the models and training methods tested in 2023.

evidence.explanation: The study reports poor transfer beyond training complexity after GPT3 fine-tuning, including multiplication. It also reports only 55% and 59% accuracy for ChatGPT and GPT4 on three-digit multiplication, supporting the observed reliability limitation.

Specialized transformers reached 95% accuracy on 35-by-3-digit multiplication after training-set priming, demonstrating meaningful progress. However, priming supplied examples at target lengths, and the study found no transfer to omitted lengths; this does not satisfy the unseen-length contradiction condition.
